title: Introduce metric-escrow buffering and adaptive trace throttle for burst-stable observability
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation:
Observability backends see large short-duration bursts from clients (prefetches, retries, synthetic tests) that cause alert storms and saturate trace ingestion. Existing burst-handling is coarse: we drop or sample traces at the ingestion tier which leads to blind spots when investigating incidents and frequent false-positive SLO alerts.

What this PR does (single-string description):
- Introduces a metric escrow service: a lightweight buffering/lease mechanism that holds short-lived high-cardinality metrics for up to a configurable window (default 30s) and emits aggregated summaries to long-term pipelines. The escrow preserves per-tenant attribution and a compact burst signature so we can reconstruct a burst without ingesting all raw samples.
- Adds an adaptive trace throttle that coordinates with the escrow service. During a surge the throttle: (1) temporarily reduces sampling of low-cost traces, (2) preserves traces flagged by the escrow as "burst anchors" (e.g., high token-cost or error-bearing), and (3) opens an on-demand trace-hydration path to fetch full payloads for selected anchors if investigators request them.
- Adds a new dashboard called "Burst Canvas" (dashboards/burst_canvas.json) that shows escrowed burst signatures, per-tenant escrow occupancy, and synthetic SLO playback overlays so SREs can replay how alert thresholds would behave under recorded bursts.
- Adds a synthetic SLO playback tool and harness (scripts/synthetic_slo_playback.py) to run recorded burst signatures against current alert rules to tune hysteresis/quiet windows without hitting production traffic.
- Adds per-tenant escrow quotas and a backpressure policy that factors token-cost and kernel-queue metrics so GPU-heavy tenants are backpressured earlier.

Review conversation (condensed into strings):
- "Luca Moreno: Great approach, can you clarify the amortized memory and cardinality growth for escrow?"
- "Author (Asha): Added an eviction + sketching layer: escrow keeps raw keys for 30s and maintains a count-min sketch for longer windows. Updated docs with memory budget formulas and a per-tenant emergency eviction policy."
- "Priya Singh: How do we avoid double-counting when escrow emits aggregated summaries and the pipeline also receives sampled raw events?"
- "Author: Escrow emits tagged summaries with escrowed=true and downstream pipelines de-dupe based on (tenant, time-window, escrow-signature) tags. Added unit tests to assert de-dupe behavior."
- "Evan Chen: We need an SLO-friendly signal for trace-hydration requests so we don't hydrate too many heavy traces during on-call investigations."
- "Author: Added a hydration-rate limiter and an investigator quota that honors oncall-mode feature flag; documented recommended values in runbook."
- "Luca Moreno: CI flaky on observability-e2e in the first run; appears unrelated but please rerun."
- "Author: Reran CI and fixed a timing race in the test harness; rebase and pushed fix commit e5f6g7."

release_notes:
- Introduced metric escrow: short-term buffering and compact burst signatures to smooth ingestion spikes.
- Added adaptive trace throttle that coordinates with escrow to prioritize high-cost/error traces and enable on-demand hydration.
- New 'Burst Canvas' dashboard and synthetic SLO playback tool for offline alert tuning.
- Feature-flag gated; opt-in rollout recommended.
